title: Field-sketching a grey hornbill in three shapes
storyboard: Film: overhead timelapse of a pencil field sketch of a grey hornbill in a journal, 10 min to 12 s

scenes.headline: Sketching a hornbill in three shapes
Egg for the body, circle for the head
scenes.body: Field sketches start loose: get the posture before any detail.

scenes.headline: Add the casque: the helmet-like ridge on top of the bill.
Date. Place. What it was doing.
scenes.body: Margin fact: a nesting hornbill mum is walled into a tree hole with mud.

caption:
Three shapes and a casque.

In most hornbill species the nest hole is closed with mud except for a small opening, through which the male passes food to the female inside.

Source: Britannica.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Storyboard: timelapse of a real camp field sketch; reference photo plus step cards make it a teachable how-to, not just a speed-draw.
